title: Where to centre a test's difficulty
statement: Where a predictive test's difficulty should be centred: on the published norm, on the actual cohort or above grade.
example: One blueprint centred its item difficulty at 200-210, so it measured most precisely well above where its students sat and an on-grade reader read as failing.
detail: A measurement review found that centring item difficulty at 200-210 puts the most information ~+1.3 logits above where students sit, so an on-grade reader reads as failing; it asked to fail blueprints centred above the verified spring mean and to reconcile with the observed cohort mean of 206.4 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0072-learnings-from-incept-map-proxy-2026-06-25.qmd`). The staged assessment standard still says to centre above grade, because a test centred at the grade median is too easy to confirm above-grade reading (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/assessment-design.md`). To settle it: the linking study that standard already calls for, in which students take this test and the published one.

evidence.quote: centering item difficulty at 200-210 (our kb-0059 "by design") maximizes info ~+1.3 logits ABOVE where students sit → makes an on-grade reader read as failing and biases logit→RIT regression.
FAIL blueprints centered above the verified spring mean; reconcile vs the observed cohort mean 206.4.
**Center above grade.** A test centered at the grade median is too easy to confirm above-grade reading.
